If you sacrifice the equipped creature to deal 1 damage to a target permanent or player, the damage is dealt by the creature as it last existed on the battlefield.

A modal double-faced card can’t be transformed or be put onto the battlefield transformed. Ignore any instruction to transform a modal double-faced card or to put one onto the battlefield transformed.
Keep careful track of how many energy counters each player has. You may do so by keeping a running count on paper, by using a die, or by any other clear and mutually agreeable method.

If a creature an opponent controls enters the battlefield at the same time that Urabrask the Hidden enters the battlefield under your control, Urabrask’s effect doesn’t apply to your opponent’s creature.

The controller of a copy can’t choose to pay any alternative or additional costs for the copy. However, effects based on any alternative or additional costs that were paid for the original spell are copied as though those same costs were paid for the copy
If you reveal your entire library and reveal fewer than X creature cards of the chosen type, you’ll put the cards of the chosen type that you did reveal onto the battlefield and shuffle your library.
This card is a Mountain and a Swamp even while in the graveyard, library, or any other zone.
It does not trigger at all if this is tapped at the start of the draw step, and it checks this again on resolution.
If the targeted creature has indestructible, it’s still a legal target — it just isn’t destroyed. The rest of Polymorph’s effect happens as normal.
Mana symbols in the text boxes of permanents you control don’t count toward your devotion to any color.
A creature card cast this way has Mulldrifter’s characteristics until it leaves the battlefield or leaves the stack other than by resolving. These characteristics are copiable values of that object.
If unpreventable damage is applied to this card, you still remove a counter even though the prevention fails.
Effects that reduce the cost of spells reduce the total cost, including any escalate costs added.
Valkmira’s last ability affects each spell (including Aura spells), activated ability, and triggered ability controlled by an opponent that targets you or another permanent you control.
Although the tokens are attacking, they never were declared as attacking creatures (for purposes of abilities that trigger whenever a creature attacks, for example).
If a spell targets Goldspan Dragon more than once, the triggered ability will trigger only once.
If you choose the first mode of Koma’s activated ability, you can choose a permanent that’s already tapped as the target. The effect stopping its activated abilities will still apply.
If the chosen creature is copying something else (for example, if the chosen creature is another Altered Ego), then your Altered Ego enters the battlefield as whatever the chosen creature copied.
Lure doesn’t give any creatures the ability to block the target creature. It just forces those creatures that are already able to block the creature to do so.
The ability will not trigger on itself entering the battlefield, but it will trigger on any other creature that is put onto the battlefield at the same time.
If an effect copies a spell multiple times, as Finale of Promise may, Ral’s first ability triggers that many times.
If an adventurer card ends up in exile for any other reason than by exiling itself while resolving, it won’t give you permission to cast it as a creature spell.

Lands are normally colorless permanents, even if they tap for mana of a certain color.

Steel Hellkite’s last ability destroys only nonland permanents whose converted mana cost is exactly equal to X, and only those controlled by players who have been dealt combat damage by Steel Hellkite this turn.

Bolster itself doesn’t target any creature, though some spells and abilities that bolster may have other effects that target creatures. For example, you could put counters on a creature with protection from white with Abzan Skycaptain’s bolster ability.
Each pile may contain from zero to five cards; they don’t have to be split “evenly.”
If you cast an artifact spell this way, it won’t be exiled if it would be put into your graveyard this turn.
Once Siege Striker’s ability has resolved, it keeps the power-and-toughness bonus even if some of the tapped creatures leave the battlefield or become untapped.
If another player gains control of Shipbreaker Kraken, the creatures will no longer be affected by the effect preventing them from untapping, even if you later regain control of Shipbreaker Kraken.

The control-change effect of Blim’s ability lasts indefinitely. It doesn’t wear off during the cleanup step, and it doesn’t expire if Blim leaves the battlefield. In a multiplayer game, it does expire if the current controller leaves the game.
Vehicle is an artifact type, not a creature type. A Vehicle that’s crewed won’t normally have any creature type.

Whether the target creature is a Knight is checked only as the equip Knight ability is activated and as that ability resolves. If the creature somehow becomes a non-Knight creature later, Steelclaw Lance remains attached to it.
If you have at least one of each of the three Urza’s lands on the battlefield, you must take the 2 mana instead of just one.
If an attacking creature has intimidate, what colors it is matters only as the defending player declares blockers. Once it’s blocked, changing its colors won’t change that.
You choose whether to discard or not on resolution. If not, then you sacrifice this card. You can choose to not discard even if you no longer control this card on resolution.
Reflector Mage’s ability doesn’t stop any player from playing lands (in the case that the returned creature was also a land).

If Descent into Madness isn’t on the battlefield when its ability resolves, use the number of counters on it when it left the battlefield to determine how many permanents and/or cards from hands to exile.
If the targeted spell is modal (that is, it says “Choose one —” or the like), you can’t choose a different mode.
You can’t choose the name of a token unless that token has the same name as a card.

In the Commander variant, a double-faced card’s color identity is determined by the mana costs and mana symbols in the rules text of both faces combined. If either face has a color indicator or basic land type, those are also considered.
If an effect allows you to play a land or cast a spell from among a group of cards, you may play or cast a modal double-faced card with any face that fits the criteria of that effect.
The companion’s other abilities apply only if the creature is on the battlefield. They have no effect while the companion is outside the game.

Kels’s middle ability is a triggered ability, not an activated ability. It doesn’t allow you to sacrifice a permanent whenever you want; rather, you need some other way of sacrificing permanents, such as Kels’s last ability.
Each player will have a chance to cast instants and activate abilities after Benefactor’s Draught’s delayed triggered abilities have resolved, before combat damage is dealt.
Once Mirage Mirror’s ability resolves, it no longer has that ability.
Effects that reduce the generic mana cost of a spell (such as that of Marauding Raptor) can’t reduce that spell’s colored mana requirements.
The current wording explicitly removes the creature from combat. It is no longer an attacking or blocking creature.
Convoke doesn’t change a spell’s mana cost or converted mana cost.

If the chosen creature is a token, Progenitor Mimic copies the original characteristics of that token as stated by the effect that put it onto the battlefield. Copying a token doesn’t make Progenitor Mimic become a token.
You may target an untapped creature with Ray of Command.
If another effect allows you to cast a split card with aftermath from any zone other than a graveyard, you can’t cast the half with aftermath.

If each player has 13 life as Triskaidekaphobia’s ability resolves, the game ends in a draw.
The choice is optional.

Lost Auramancers doesn’t have to have been sacrificed as part of the vanishing ability for its last ability to trigger. It will trigger no matter why it was put into a graveyard from the battlefield, as long as it had no time counters on it at the time.
Heroic abilities will trigger only once per spell, even if that spell targets the creature with the heroic ability multiple times.

In a multiplayer game, the targeted opponent may choose what information to share with others if that player wants advice on how to split the cards, but that player doesn’t have to share any information at all.

When a land enters the battlefield under your control, each landfall ability of the permanents you control will trigger. You can put them on the stack in any order. The last ability you put on the stack will be the first one that resolves.
Vesuvan Doppelganger copies the mana cost of the creature it’s copying but doesn’t copy its color.
Loses a counter even if it is affected by a Fog-like effect which prevents it from dealing damage.
Turning a permanent face up or face down doesn’t change whether that permanent is tapped or untapped.

If Blood on the Snow is copied, no mana was spent to cast the copy, so you can return only a creature or planeswalker card with converted mana cost 0.

This ability is paid for during the declare attackers step of the combat phase.

The ability is mandatory. If you control at least one other creature when the ability resolves, you must sacrifice one. If you don’t control any other creatures at that time, the ability won’t do anything.
Lich’s Mirror has no effect if a spell or ability (such as the one from Helix Pinnacle) states that a player “wins the game.” If a player wins the game, the game ends immediately.
If a creature on the battlefield or a creature card in a graveyard has {X} in its mana cost, X is considered to be 0.
The mana cost and converted mana cost of strive spells don’t change no matter how many targets they have. Strive abilities affect only what you pay.
If the first triggered ability of suspend (the one that removes time counters) is countered, no time counter is removed. The ability will trigger again during the card’s owner’s next upkeep.

Auras attached to the exiled creature will be put into their owners’ graveyards. Equipment attached to the exiled creature will become unattached and remain on the battlefield. Any counters on the exiled creature will cease to exist.
If a player rolls {CHAOS}, both chaos abilities will trigger. The player may put those abilities on the stack in any order.

Exiling a card with suspend isn’t casting that card. This action doesn’t use the stack and can’t be responded to.
This is the timeshifted version of Concentrate.
If you don’t have two cards of the right color in your hand, you can’t choose to cast the spell using the alternative cost.
Both commanders start in the command zone, and the remaining 98 cards (or 58 cards in a Commander Draft game) of your deck are shuffled to become your library.
You don’t choose whether the target artifact creature gains flying, trample, or haste until Golem Artisan’s second ability resolves.
Kuldotha Forgemaster can be one of the three artifacts you sacrifice to activate the ability.
This has basic land types, but it isn’t a basic land. Things that affect basic lands don’t affect it. Things that affect basic land types do.
If a manifested creature would have morph if it were face up, you may also turn it face up by paying its morph cost.
If the target creature is an illegal target by the time Path of Peace tries to resolve, the spell doesn’t resolve. No player gains life.

Players may cast any number of creature spells plus one noncreature spell each turn.

Frogify may enchant a permanent that is only temporarily a creature, such as a Vehicle. If this happens, Frogify’s effect causes the enchanted permanent to remain a 1/1 blue Frog creature even after the temporary effect expires.
If a permanent has {X} in its mana cost, X is considered to be 0.
If the creature leaves the battlefield, the exiled card will no longer be encoded on any creature. It will stay exiled.
If a card in your library has {X} in its mana cost, X is considered to be 0.

Each split card is a single card. For example, if you discard one, you’ve discarded one card, not two. If an effect counts the number of instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard, Destined // Lead counts once, not twice.
The last ability triggers whenever you play a land and also whenever a land enters the battlefield under your control for some other reason, such as the ability of Into the Wilds.

Effects that modify the power or toughness of the land creature without setting it will apply to its new base power and toughness no matter when they started to take effect. The same is true for counters that change its power and toughness.

A spell cast using jump-start will always be exiled afterward, whether it resolves, it’s countered, or it leaves the stack in some other way.
